---
title: "Transportation Choices"
subtitle: "Share of population within 1/4 mile of a bike or transit facility, by scenario"
date: today
---

## Purpose

How much of the Wasatch Front's population lives somewhere they can actually *choose* to bike or take transit instead of drive? Transportation Choices answers that with one number per place: the percent of people within 1/4 mile of a dedicated bike facility, or of a frequent bus route, transit stop, or station.

That number only means something next to a point of comparison, so we compute it for three scenarios. Each scenario is a combination of two independent inputs that do **not** have to match: a socioeconomic (SE) forecast year, and a GIS facility *vintage* year (what's actually built on the ground, or assumed built, as of some year).

| Scenario | SE year | GIS vintage | Reads as |
|------------------|------------------|------------------|------------------|
| Existing 2027 | 2027 | 2027 | today |
| No Build 2055 | 2055 | 2032 | 2055's population, with no further facilities built |
| RTP (Build) 2055 | 2055 | 2055 | 2055's population, with the RTP's planned facilities built |

Comparing No Build against RTP isolates the effect of *building the plan* -- same future population, different infrastructure. Comparing Existing against either 2055 scenario shows how much of that effect is just growth.

::: callout-important
## The 2032 GIS vintage is a placeholder, not real data

Neither mode has a real 2032 facility layer yet -- bike is waiting on a layer from Sarah/Hugh (via Suzie), transit on a LIN Stops file from Suzie. Until those arrive, 2032 is deliberately defined as "unchanged from 2027" (see `GIS_VINTAGES` below), so **No Build 2055 currently only isolates the effect of population growth, not a true no-further-investment scenario.** Re-run this page once the real 2032 data lands.
:::

GIS facility data is *incremental* by vintage year and mode: each vintage layers new facilities on top of the previous one rather than restating everything from scratch. That's what makes the pipeline easy to extend -- adding a scenario is one line in `SCENARIOS`, and adding a GIS vintage is one entry in `GIS_VINTAGES`.

This replaces the `_archive/` v9 arcpy scripts (01-08), which bundled SE and facility data together per scenario (so SE year and GIS vintage couldn't vary independently) and filtered transit stops with a hardcoded route list.

## Data Sources

| Mode | Vintage | What's added | Source |
|------------------|------------------|------------------|------------------|
| Bike | 2027 (base) | On-street bike facilities + trails | `utah_bikeways`, filtered to `Facility1` excluding "Not Available" and the class-3 shared-roadway/shoulder family |
| Bike | 2032 | *(placeholder -- not yet available)* | TBD, Sarah/Hugh via Suzie |
| Bike | 2055 | RTP 2027 Preferred Scenario AT projects, line facilities only | `at_line_projects` |
| Transit | 2027 (base) | Fixed-guideway stations + frequent bus stops | `uta_stops` + `uta_routes` |
| Transit | 2032 | *(placeholder -- unchanged from 2027)* | LIN Stops, not yet received from Suzie |
| Transit | 2055 | RTP 2027 Preferred Scenario transit projects, filtered to LRT/CRT/streetcar rail and high-frequency bus (BRT, Enhanced Bus) | `transit_line_projects`, `transit_point_projects` |

Socioeconomic data is WFRC's v10 forecast, one CSV per year (2023-2065) under `_data/raw/SE_v10_20260921/`. TAZ geometry comes from the `WasatchFrontTAZ` REST service (`wftcm_taz`).

## Setup

Two dictionaries carry all of the above as data rather than as logic: `GIS_VINTAGES` encodes what each vintage adds and which earlier vintage it builds on, and `SCENARIOS` just points at a `(se_year, gis_year)` pair for each named scenario. Nothing downstream needs to change to add a scenario or a vintage -- only these two structures do.

```{python}
#| label: setup

from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd
import geopandas as gpd
from gis_adhoc_analyses.layer_cache import ensure_layers

PATHS = {
    "se_dir": Path("_data/raw/SE_v10_20260921"),
    "output": Path("output"),
}

CRS = "EPSG:26912"  # UTM 12N, meters -- project everything to this before buffering/intersecting

CONSTANTS = {
    "buffer_m": 0.25 * 1609.34,  # 0.25 mi in meters
    "wfrc_county_fips": [3, 11, 35, 57],  # Box Elder, Davis, Salt Lake, Weber
    "se_join_field": "TAZID",
}

# Incremental by vintage year: "adds" are layer keys new at that vintage,
# "builds_on" is the vintage it layers on top of (None = base vintage).
GIS_VINTAGES = {
    "bike": {
        2027: {"adds": ["utah_bikeways"], "builds_on": None},
        2032: {"adds": [], "builds_on": 2027},  # placeholder: layer TBD (Sarah/Hugh via Suzie)
        2055: {"adds": ["at_line_projects"], "builds_on": 2032},
    },
    "transit": {
        2027: {"adds": ["uta_stops", "uta_routes"], "builds_on": None},
        2032: {"adds": [], "builds_on": 2027},  # placeholder: treat as unchanged from 2027
        # until LIN Stops (Suzie) arrives -- a deliberate interim choice, not a gap
        2055: {"adds": ["transit_line_projects", "transit_point_projects"], "builds_on": 2032},
    },
}

SCENARIOS = [
    {"name": "existing_2027", "se_year": 2027, "gis_year": 2027},
    {"name": "no_build_2055", "se_year": 2055, "gis_year": 2032},
    {"name": "rtp_2055", "se_year": 2055, "gis_year": 2055},
]
```

## Data Acquisition

Every REST layer any vintage needs gets fetched once, up front, by reading the keys straight out of `GIS_VINTAGES` -- add a layer to a vintage and it's automatically requested here too.

```{python}
#| label: fetch-rest-layers

rest_keys = sorted(
    {"wftcm_taz"}
    | {layer for mode in GIS_VINTAGES.values() for v in mode.values() for layer in v["adds"]}
)
L = ensure_layers(rest_keys)
print(f"Fetched {len(L)} REST layers: {rest_keys}")
```

```{python}
#| label: check-se-years

se_years_available = sorted(
    int(p.stem.removeprefix("SE_")) for p in PATHS["se_dir"].glob("SE_*.csv")
)
assert se_years_available, f"No SE files found under {PATHS['se_dir']}"
for scenario in SCENARIOS:
    assert scenario["se_year"] in se_years_available, (
        f"Scenario {scenario['name']!r} needs SE_{scenario['se_year']}.csv -- not found"
    )
print(
    f"SE years available: {se_years_available[0]}-{se_years_available[-1]} ({len(se_years_available)} files)"
)
print("All scenario SE years present.")
```

::: callout-note
## Geography levels beyond region and county

The v9 pipeline summarized results by workshop area as well as region and county. The `wftcm_taz` layer's `CITYGRP` field reproduces that same workshop-area breakdown (its values -- "Northern Salt Lake County," "Southwest Salt Lake County," "Southern Weber County," etc. -- line up with the v9 script's `SmallArea` boundary names), so it's used here as `WorkshopArea`. The layer's WFTDM district fields (`DISTLRG`/`DISTMED`/`DISTSML`) add three more levels of their own -- `CityName`, `DistrictLarge`, `DistrictMedium`, and `DistrictSmall` -- all without needing a separate boundary source. (`DISTSUPER`/`DSUP_NAME` also exists on the layer, but within the WFRC footprint it's identical to `CountyName`, so it isn't added as its own level.)
:::

## Build Facility Geometry — Bike {#sec-bike-geometry}

Bike facilities are line geometry, buffered directly: `utah_bikeways`'s `Facility1` field distinguishes facility type, encoded with AGRC's 1/2/3 bikeway class suffixes (1 = physically separated cycle track, 2 = bike lane, 3 = shared roadway/shoulder). `"Not Available"` means no bike facility at all, but the class-3 family (`"Other bike route, unspecified (3)"`, `"Shoulder bikeway (3A)"`, `"Marked shared roadway (3B)"`, `"Signed shared roadway (3C)"`) is excluded too -- it's just a stripe or sign on a road shared with traffic, not a dedicated facility, and the v9 `_archive/` script excluded the same codes (`bike_l`/`bike_r NOT IN ('3','3A','3B','3C')`). Everything else -- bike lanes, buffered/protected cycle tracks, and trails -- is existing network. The 2055 vintage adds the RTP 2027 Preferred Scenario's active-transportation **line** projects as-is -- every row in `at_line_projects` is already a bike path facility type (shared-use path, trail, bike lane, sidepath, etc.), matching `utah_bikeways`'s own facility categories. The companion point layer (`at_point_projects`) is pedestrian/bike crossings, not bike-path segments, so it's excluded here -- `WFRCAnalytics/GIS-RTP-Phasing-Criteria` treats those crossings as a separate network-connectivity attribute rather than part of the facility network.

```{python}
#| label: bike-raw-by-vintage

# Excludes "Not Available" (no facility) and the class-3 shared-roadway/shoulder
# family -- not a dedicated facility, matching the v9 _archive/ script's
# bike_l/bike_r NOT IN ('3','3A','3B','3C') exclusion.
_BIKE_EXCLUDED_FACILITY1_SQL = (
    "'Not Available','Other bike route, unspecified (3)','Shoulder bikeway (3A)',"
    "'Marked shared roadway (3B)','Signed shared roadway (3C)'"
)

bike_raw = {
    2027: gpd.read_file(
        L["utah_bikeways"],
        where=f"Facility1 IS NOT NULL AND Facility1 NOT IN ({_BIKE_EXCLUDED_FACILITY1_SQL})",
    ).to_crs(CRS)[["geometry"]],
    2032: gpd.GeoDataFrame(geometry=[], crs=CRS),  # placeholder: 2032 bike layer TBD
    2055: gpd.read_file(L["at_line_projects"]).to_crs(CRS)[["geometry"]],
}
for year, gdf in bike_raw.items():
    print(f"Bike {year} adds: {len(gdf)} features")
```

Each vintage's cumulative network is its own `adds` plus everything the vintage it `builds_on` already had -- so a vintage with nothing new yet (2032, for now) is simply identical to the vintage beneath it, not empty. Buffering and dissolving that cumulative network once per vintage gives the geometry every scenario needing that vintage can reuse.

```{python}
#| label: bike-buffers-by-vintage

bike_cum = {}
for year in sorted(GIS_VINTAGES["bike"]):
    builds_on = GIS_VINTAGES["bike"][year]["builds_on"]
    parts = [bike_raw[year]] if builds_on is None else [bike_cum[builds_on], bike_raw[year]]
    bike_cum[year] = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
        pd.concat(parts, ignore_index=True), geometry="geometry", crs=CRS
    )

bike_buffers = {
    year: gpd.GeoDataFrame(geometry=[cum.buffer(CONSTANTS["buffer_m"]).union_all()], crs=CRS)
    for year, cum in bike_cum.items()
}
for year, cum in bike_cum.items():
    print(f"Bike {year} cumulative: {len(cum)} features")
```

## Build Facility Geometry — Transit {#sec-transit-geometry}

Transit works differently in a way that matters for the buffer, not just the source. The 2027 base is built entirely from **stop/station points**, and only from a *subset* of stops --

1.  LRT/CRT fixed-guideway stations, caught by `mode` containing `TRAX` or `FrontRunner`, and
2.  **frequent bus stops only** -- `uta_routes` filtered to the frequent/fixed-guideway service tiers, matched back to stops through the comma-separated `route` field.

(The 2055 vintage below does add route linework -- planned corridors buffered as lines, same as bike -- once it's clear a single centroid point badly undercounts a corridor's real coverage.)

Every other bus stop is excluded. This two-part filter replaces v9's hardcoded route list with something that updates itself as UTA's service changes.

```{python}
#| label: transit-2027-base

_HF_ROUTETYPES_SQL = "'Frequent','BRT','Blue Line','Red Line','Green Line','S Line','FrontRunner'"
hf_route_abbrs = set(
    gpd.read_file(L["uta_routes"], where=f"routetype IN ({_HF_ROUTETYPES_SQL})")["lineabbr"].astype(
        str
    )
)

stops_raw = gpd.read_file(L["uta_stops"]).to_crs(CRS)
fixed_guideway = stops_raw[stops_raw["mode"].str.contains("TRAX|FrontRunner|BRT", na=False)]
hf_routes = stops_raw[
    stops_raw["route"].apply(
        lambda r: (
            False if pd.isna(r) else bool({t.strip() for t in str(r).split(",")} & hf_route_abbrs)
        )
    )
]
transit_2027 = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
    pd.concat(
        [fixed_guideway[["geometry"]], hf_routes[["geometry"]]], ignore_index=True
    ).drop_duplicates(),
    geometry="geometry",
    crs=CRS,
)
print(f"Fixed-guideway / BRT stops: {len(fixed_guideway)}")
print(f"Frequent-route stops:      {len(hf_routes)}")
print(f"Transit 2027 base (dedup): {len(transit_2027)}")
```

The 2055 vintage adds the RTP's transit projects. A planned rail or BRT corridor arrives as a line, not a point, but reducing it to a single centroid badly undercounts its real catchment -- a corridor has stations spaced along its whole length, not clustered at its midpoint. Reasonableness-checking against the v9 benchmark confirmed this: collapsing lines to centroids put RTP 2050-equivalent transit coverage around 20%, far under the v9 pipeline's reported 33% for 2050 RTP. So line projects are buffered directly as corridors here, the same way bike line facilities already are, while point projects (new stations) stay point-buffered.

::: callout-note
## Full-line buffering is an interim choice, not the final answer

Buffering a corridor's entire length overshoots too, in the other direction -- it assumes a station is reachable from every point along the line, when real stations are discrete and spaced out (rail stops are often a mile or more apart), leaving real gaps that a full-line buffer doesn't capture. Against the v9 benchmark this currently reads ~45% versus the reported 33% for 2050 RTP, roughly as far over as the centroid approach was under. The correct fix is what `WFRCAnalytics/GIS-RTP-Phasing-Criteria` already does: buffer each line, intersect with the real 2055 UF TDM model's stop nodes to get actual station locations, then apply mode-specific buffer tiers (Rail 0.5 mi, BRT 0.35 mi, Core 0.25 mi). That needs the TDM network GDB, which isn't available in this repo yet -- full-line buffering is the deliberate placeholder until it is.
:::

Not every project qualifies, though: only LRT/CRT/streetcar rail and high-frequency bus (BRT, Enhanced Bus) project types count toward this mode, mirroring the Rail/BRT buffer-tier grouping `WFRCAnalytics/GIS-RTP-Phasing-Criteria` uses (which buffers FrontRunner, TRAX, and the Sugar House Streetcar together as one fixed-guideway-equivalent tier, separate from core local bus). Exploratory corridors, corridor preservation, transit/mobility hubs, maintenance facilities, park & rides, and gondolas are excluded -- they aren't LRT/CRT/high-frequency-bus stops themselves.

```{python}
#| label: transit-raw-by-vintage

# RTP project types that count as LRT/CRT/streetcar rail or high-frequency bus --
# excludes exploratory corridors, corridor preservation, transit/mobility hubs,
# maintenance facilities, park & rides, and gondolas (see prose above).
_TRANSIT_LINE_TYPES_SQL = "'Light Rail','Commuter Rail','Street Car','Bus Rapid Transit','Enhanced Bus'"
_TRANSIT_POINT_TYPES_SQL = "'New Station'"

transit_2055_lines = gpd.read_file(
    L["transit_line_projects"], where=f"improvement_type IN ({_TRANSIT_LINE_TYPES_SQL})"
).to_crs(CRS)
transit_2055_points = gpd.read_file(
    L["transit_point_projects"], where=f"improvement_type IN ({_TRANSIT_POINT_TYPES_SQL})"
).to_crs(CRS)
transit_raw = {
    2027: transit_2027,
    2032: gpd.GeoDataFrame(geometry=[], crs=CRS),  # placeholder: LIN Stops file from Suzie
    2055: gpd.GeoDataFrame(
        pd.concat(
            [transit_2055_points[["geometry"]], transit_2055_lines[["geometry"]]],
            ignore_index=True,
        ),
        geometry="geometry",
        crs=CRS,
    ),
}
for year, gdf in transit_raw.items():
    print(f"Transit {year} adds: {len(gdf)} features")
```

```{python}
#| label: transit-buffers-by-vintage

transit_cum = {}
for year in sorted(GIS_VINTAGES["transit"]):
    builds_on = GIS_VINTAGES["transit"][year]["builds_on"]
    parts = (
        [transit_raw[year]] if builds_on is None else [transit_cum[builds_on], transit_raw[year]]
    )
    transit_cum[year] = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
        pd.concat(parts, ignore_index=True), geometry="geometry", crs=CRS
    )

transit_buffers = {
    year: gpd.GeoDataFrame(geometry=[cum.buffer(CONSTANTS["buffer_m"]).union_all()], crs=CRS)
    for year, cum in transit_cum.items()
}
for year, cum in transit_cum.items():
    print(f"Transit {year} cumulative: {len(cum)} features")
```

## Prepare TAZ Geography

TAZ geometry itself doesn't change across scenarios -- only the population joined onto it does (that happens in @sec-compute, per scenario). So this runs once: filter to the four WFRC counties, and add the fields every downstream calculation needs -- `Region` (a constant, for the region-level rollup), the geography breakdowns (`CountyName`, `WorkshopArea`, `CityName`, and the WFTDM district hierarchy), and each TAZ's total area in acres. These all come straight off fields already on the TAZ layer (`CITYGRP`, `DISTLRG`/`DISTMED`/`DISTSML`), so there's no separate boundary source to fetch or maintain.

```{python}
#| label: prepare-taz

taz_raw = gpd.read_file(L["wftcm_taz"]).to_crs(CRS)
print(f"TAZ columns: {list(taz_raw.columns)}")

taz = taz_raw[taz_raw["CO_FIPS"].isin(CONSTANTS["wfrc_county_fips"])].copy()
taz["Region"] = "WFRC"
taz["CountyName"] = taz["CO_NAME"].str.title()
taz["WorkshopArea"] = taz["CITYGRP"].replace("", pd.NA)  # blank = not assigned to a workshop area
taz["CityName"] = taz["CITY_NAME"]
taz["DistrictLarge"] = taz["DLRG_NAME"]
taz["DistrictMedium"] = taz["DMED_NAME"]
taz["DistrictSmall"] = taz["DSML_NAME"]
taz["AcresTotal"] = taz.geometry.area / 4046.8564224
print(f"TAZ after county filter: {len(taz)} (from {len(taz_raw)})")
for col in ["CountyName", "WorkshopArea", "CityName", "DistrictLarge", "DistrictMedium", "DistrictSmall"]:
    print(f"  {col}: {taz[col].nunique()} unique, {taz[col].isna().sum()} null")
```

## Compute Compatible-Area % by Scenario {#sec-compute}

We don't know how population is distributed *within* a TAZ, only its total -- so where a facility buffer only partly covers a TAZ, we assume population spreads evenly across the TAZ's area and credit that TAZ with the same share of its population: `HHPOPPiece = HHPOP * (piece area / total area)`. Summing `HHPOPPiece` over all pieces and dividing by total `HHPOP` for a geography gives the percent of its population within 1/4 mile of a facility -- which is exactly `SCENARIOS × modes × geography levels` worth of one number each, so the result is a single tidy table rather than the nine separate CSVs the old per-scenario scripts produced.

```{python}
#| label: compute-tidy-results

GEOGRAPHY_LEVELS = [
    "Region",
    "CountyName",
    "WorkshopArea",
    "CityName",
    "DistrictLarge",
    "DistrictMedium",
    "DistrictSmall",
]

results = []
for scenario in SCENARIOS:
    se_path = PATHS["se_dir"] / f"SE_{scenario['se_year']}.csv"
    assert se_path.is_file(), f"Missing SE file: {se_path}"
    se = pd.read_csv(se_path)
    se.columns = se.columns.str.lstrip(";")  # v10 export has a stray leading ';' on the header row

    taz_se = taz.merge(
        se[[CONSTANTS["se_join_field"], "HHPOP"]], on=CONSTANTS["se_join_field"], how="left"
    )

    for mode, buffers in (("bike", bike_buffers), ("transit", transit_buffers)):
        pieces = gpd.overlay(taz_se, buffers[scenario["gis_year"]], how="intersection")
        pieces["AcresPiece"] = pieces.geometry.area / 4046.8564224
        pieces["HHPOPPiece"] = pieces["HHPOP"] * pieces["AcresPiece"] / pieces["AcresTotal"]

        for level in GEOGRAPHY_LEVELS:
            totals = taz_se.groupby(level)["HHPOP"].sum()
            piece_totals = (
                pieces.groupby(level)["HHPOPPiece"].sum().reindex(totals.index, fill_value=0)
            )
            # Overlay geometry area can round-trip a hair above the true total
            # (e.g. 1.0000000000000004) due to floating-point noise in the
            # intersection -- clip rather than let it fail the sanity check below.
            pct = (piece_totals / totals).clip(upper=1.0)
            for geography_name, value in pct.items():
                results.append(
                    {
                        "scenario": scenario["name"],
                        "mode": mode,
                        "se_year": scenario["se_year"],
                        "gis_year": scenario["gis_year"],
                        "geography_level": level,
                        "geography_name": geography_name,
                        "pct_near_facility": value,
                    }
                )

tidy = pd.DataFrame(results)
print(f"Tidy results: {len(tidy)} rows")

# A handful of fine-grained geographies (e.g. Great Salt Lake open-water districts)
# have zero households, so their share-of-population is undefined (0/0 = NaN) --
# that's a legitimate result, not a bug, so it's excluded from the range check below.
n_undefined = tidy["pct_near_facility"].isna().sum()
if n_undefined:
    zero_pop_geos = sorted(
        tidy.loc[tidy["pct_near_facility"].isna(), "geography_name"].unique()
    )
    print(f"NOTE: {n_undefined} rows have undefined pct (zero-population geography): {zero_pop_geos}")

assert tidy["pct_near_facility"].dropna().between(0, 1).all(), (
    "Percentage outside [0, 1] -- check overlay/weighting"
)
tidy.head()
```

## Outputs

One CSV per scenario, each long-format across modes and geography levels -- easier for a planner to open and filter than nine narrow files, and named so each scenario's file is unambiguous on its own. A combined file across all three scenarios is also saved for the interactive charts below to read directly.

```{python}
#| label: write-outputs

PATHS["output"].mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
for scenario in SCENARIOS:
    out_path = PATHS["output"] / f"transportation_choices_{scenario['name']}.csv"
    tidy[tidy["scenario"] == scenario["name"]].to_csv(out_path, index=False)
    print(f"Saved -> {out_path}")

tidy_out_path = PATHS["output"] / "transportation_choices_tidy.csv"
tidy.to_csv(tidy_out_path, index=False)
print(f"Saved -> {tidy_out_path}")
```

## Visualization

No Build 2055 and RTP 2055 are **alternate futures**, not consecutive years -- both branch from the same Existing 2027 baseline, so each chart draws two separate lines per geography forking from that shared starting point: dashed for No Build, solid for RTP. Pick a geography level below (region, county, workshop area, city, or large/medium/small WFTDM district), then which geographies at that level to plot and which of the two 2055 scenarios to show -- Bike and Transit live in separate tabs underneath, both driven by the same controls. The gray line is always the WFRC region, so any geography reads directly against the regional reference rather than in isolation. Hover any point for its exact value.

```{ojs}
//| label: load-tidy-data
//| echo: false

// Read client-side via FileAttachment rather than ojs_define() -- the
// combination of ojs_define's embedded <script type="ojs-define"> data with
// this page's panel-tabset layout left tc_data undefined at runtime for
// every dependent cell. WFRCAnalytics/TDM-VAL-SchoolCollegeEnrollment uses
// FileAttachment for all of its interactive pages, including ones with the
// same panel-tabset/panel-input layout, so this follows that precedent
// instead of re-diagnosing the ojs_define interaction further.
tc_data = FileAttachment("output/transportation_choices_tidy.csv").csv({typed: true})
```

```{ojs}
//| label: ojs-setup
//| echo: false

// Existing 2027 is the single shared baseline; No Build 2055 and RTP 2055
// are two ALTERNATE futures branching from it, not a sequence -- so the
// x-axis is real years (2027, 2055), and each entity gets two line
// segments both starting at the same 2027 point, styled by path (dashed =
// No Build, solid = RTP) rather than laid out as one continuous timeline.
PATH_STYLE = ({
  "No Build": {dash: "5,4", label: "No Build 2055"},
  "RTP": {dash: null, label: "RTP (Build) 2055"},
})
SCENARIO_OPTIONS = Object.keys(PATH_STYLE)

REGION_COLOR = "#7f7a76" // brand wfrc-gray -- dashed/solid reference lines, deliberately neutral
INK = "#023c5b" // brand wfrc-blue

// Brand colors (_extensions/.../brand.yml) validated for CVD-safe separation
// (scripts/validate_palette.js from the dataviz skill) cover a handful of
// entities cleanly; d3's Tableau10 extends the palette for geography levels
// with more selections (e.g. large districts) without hand-picking more
// brand colors.
BRAND_PALETTE = ["#3762ad", "#c98b3a", "#a3423c", "#799f4c"]
function colorPalette(n) {
  const base = [...BRAND_PALETTE, ...d3.schemeTableau10]
  return Array.from({length: n}, (_, i) => base[i % base.length])
}

// Reshape {scenario, pct_near_facility} rows into {entity, path, year, value}
// fork segments: one "No Build" segment and one "RTP" segment per entity,
// both anchored at the same 2027 value.
function branchRows(modeKey, geoLevel, namesFilter) {
  const rows = tc_data.filter(
    (d) => d.mode === modeKey && d.geography_level === geoLevel && (!namesFilter || namesFilter.includes(d.geography_name))
  )
  const existing = new Map(rows.filter((d) => d.scenario === "existing_2027").map((d) => [d.geography_name, d.pct_near_facility]))
  const out = []
  for (const [scenarioKey, path] of [["no_build_2055", "No Build"], ["rtp_2055", "RTP"]]) {
    for (const d of rows.filter((d) => d.scenario === scenarioKey)) {
      const start = existing.get(d.geography_name)
      if (start === undefined) continue
      out.push({entity: d.geography_name, path, year: 2027, value: start})
      out.push({entity: d.geography_name, path, year: 2055, value: d.pct_near_facility})
    }
  }
  return out
}
```

```{ojs}
//| label: geo-names-source

geoNamesForLevel = [...new Set(
  tc_data
    .filter((d) => d.geography_level === selectedGeoLevel && d.geography_name != null)
    .map((d) => d.geography_name)
)].sort()

// Re-derived every time selectedGeoLevel changes, so this picker's default
// resets automatically. Small levels (region, county, workshop area) start
// fully selected like before; levels with dozens of districts start empty --
// showing 50+ lines at once isn't a readable chart, so the user opts in.
geoNamesDefault = geoNamesForLevel.length <= 12 ? geoNamesForLevel : []
```

```{ojs}
//| label: chart-fn
//| echo: false

function modeChart(modeKey, subtitle) {
  const isRegionLevel = selectedGeoLevel === "Region"
  const entityNames = isRegionLevel ? [] : selectedGeoNames
  const palette = colorPalette(entityNames.length)
  const entityColor = new Map(entityNames.map((name, i) => [name, palette[i]]))

  // The gray WFRC reference line is always drawn; when Region itself is the
  // selected level there's nothing else to plot, so entityRows is simply
  // empty and the chart reduces to that one reference line.
  const entityRows = branchRows(modeKey, selectedGeoLevel, entityNames).filter((d) => selectedPaths.includes(d.path))
  const regionRows = branchRows(modeKey, "Region", null).filter((d) => selectedPaths.includes(d.path))

  const regionAll = branchRows(modeKey, "Region", null)
  const regionNoBuild2055 = regionAll.find((d) => d.path === "No Build" && d.year === 2055)?.value
  const regionRtp2055 = regionAll.find((d) => d.path === "RTP" && d.year === 2055)?.value
  const showDelta = selectedPaths.includes("No Build") && selectedPaths.includes("RTP") && regionNoBuild2055 !== undefined && regionRtp2055 !== undefined
  const deltaPp = showDelta ? (regionRtp2055 - regionNoBuild2055) * 100 : null

  const pathCaptions = {
    "No Build": "Dashed = No Build 2055",
    "RTP": "Solid = RTP (Build) 2055",
  }
  const caption = `${selectedPaths.map((p) => pathCaptions[p]).join(" · ")} · both branch from the same 2027 baseline. Source: WFRC Transportation Choices (v10).`

  return Plot.plot({
    width,
    height: 380,
    marginRight: 130,
    marginBottom: 46,
    style: {background: "#fbf9f4", fontFamily: "Poppins, sans-serif", color: INK},
    subtitle,
    caption,
    x: {domain: [2026, 2059], ticks: [2027, 2055], label: "Year", tickFormat: "d"},
    y: {percent: true, grid: true, nice: true, label: "% within 1/4 mile ↑"},
    color: entityNames.length ? {domain: entityNames, range: palette, legend: true} : undefined,
    marks: [
      Plot.ruleY([0], {stroke: "#00000022"}),
      ...selectedPaths.flatMap((path) => [
        Plot.line(entityRows.filter((d) => d.path === path), {
          x: "year",
          y: "value",
          z: "entity",
          stroke: "entity",
          strokeWidth: path === "RTP" ? 2.5 : 2,
          strokeDasharray: PATH_STYLE[path].dash,
          strokeOpacity: path === "RTP" ? 1 : 0.8,
        }),
        Plot.line(regionRows.filter((d) => d.path === path), {
          x: "year",
          y: "value",
          stroke: REGION_COLOR,
          strokeWidth: path === "RTP" ? 3 : 2.5,
          strokeDasharray: PATH_STYLE[path].dash,
        }),
      ]),
      Plot.dot(entityRows, {
        x: "year",
        y: "value",
        fill: "entity",
        r: 3.5,
        tip: true,
        channels: {Geography: "entity", Scenario: (d) => (d.year === 2027 ? "Existing 2027" : PATH_STYLE[d.path].label)},
      }),
      Plot.dot(regionRows, {
        x: "year",
        y: "value",
        fill: REGION_COLOR,
        r: 4,
        tip: true,
        channels: {Geography: () => "WFRC region", Scenario: (d) => (d.year === 2027 ? "Existing 2027" : PATH_STYLE[d.path].label)},
      }),
      Plot.text(entityRows.filter((d) => d.path === (selectedPaths.includes("RTP") ? "RTP" : selectedPaths[0]) && d.year === 2055), {
        x: "year",
        y: "value",
        text: (d) => d.entity,
        dx: 10,
        textAnchor: "start",
        fontWeight: 600,
        fill: (d) => entityColor.get(d.entity),
      }),
      Plot.text(regionRows.filter((d) => d.path === (selectedPaths.includes("RTP") ? "RTP" : selectedPaths[0]) && d.year === 2055), {
        x: "year",
        y: "value",
        text: () => "WFRC region",
        dx: 10,
        dy: 16,
        textAnchor: "start",
        fontStyle: "italic",
        fill: REGION_COLOR,
      }),
      Plot.text(deltaPp === null ? [] : [{year: 2055, value: (regionNoBuild2055 + regionRtp2055) / 2}], {
        x: "year",
        y: "value",
        dx: 10,
        dy: -28,
        text: () => `${deltaPp >= 0 ? "+" : ""}${deltaPp.toFixed(1)} pp, RTP vs No Build`,
        fontWeight: 700,
        fontSize: 12,
        fill: INK,
      }),
    ],
  })
}
```

::: callout-note
## Known rough edges

This is a first pass, not a final design: colors are tuned for light mode only (no separate dark-mode palette yet), the fork layout hardcodes `existing_2027`/`no_build_2055`/`rtp_2055` as the three scenario names (adding a fourth scenario -- e.g. a second "build" alternative -- needs `branchRows()` updated, not just `SCENARIOS`), the "pp vs No Build" annotation and entity end-labels quietly disappear rather than erroring if a scenario checkbox is unchecked, and unchecking both scenario checkboxes leaves a blank chart (axes only, every line and point -- including the Existing 2027 baseline -- disappears with it) rather than a message explaining why.
:::

### At a Glance

The region-level headline from the charts above, as a static summary -- easier to screenshot, print, or drop into a slide than an interactive chart. Saved to `output/region_pct.png`, which the repo homepage also embeds directly, so it's the same image in both places, not a separate one.

```{python}
#| label: fig-region-pct
#| fig-cap: "Share of WFRC-region population within 1/4 mile of a bike or transit facility: Existing 2027 versus the two alternative 2055 futures, No Build and RTP."
#| fig-alt: "Bar chart with Existing 2027 set apart on the left and No Build 2055 / RTP 2055 grouped together on the right under a bracket reading '2055 -- two alternative futures'. Bike reaches 66% in 2027, 63% under No Build, and 90% under RTP. Transit reaches 19% in 2027 and No Build, rising to 45% under RTP."

import matplotlib
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

matplotlib.rcParams["font.family"] = "Poppins"  # matches center-buildout-capacity's branding

region = tidy[tidy["geography_level"] == "Region"].copy()
scenario_order = [s["name"] for s in SCENARIOS]
scenario_labels = {
    "existing_2027": "Existing\n2027",
    "no_build_2055": "No Build\n2055",
    "rtp_2055": "RTP\n2055",
}
region["scenario"] = pd.Categorical(region["scenario"], categories=scenario_order, ordered=True)
region = region.sort_values("scenario")

MODE_COLORS = {
    "bike": "#036fa8",
    "transit": "#9d4879",
}  # brand blue / rtp-fuschia -- fixed order, not cycled
INK = "#023c5b"  # brand wfrc-blue
BG = "#fbf9f4"  # matches the interactive charts above

bike_existing = region.query("mode == 'bike' and scenario == 'existing_2027'")[
    "pct_near_facility"
].iloc[0]
transit_existing = region.query("mode == 'transit' and scenario == 'existing_2027'")[
    "pct_near_facility"
].iloc[0]

# Editorial bar-chart treatment: headline + deck above the chart, direct
# value labels on each bar instead of a y-axis, an inline color key instead
# of a boxed legend, and a small source caption -- no gridlines or borders
# competing with the numbers themselves.
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.5, 5.5))
fig.patch.set_facecolor(BG)
ax.set_facecolor(BG)
fig.subplots_adjust(top=0.76, bottom=0.16, left=0.03, right=0.97)

bar_width = 0.32
# Existing 2027 sits apart on its own; No Build and RTP sit close together
# as a pair -- uneven spacing (not evenly-spaced ticks) so the layout itself
# signals "one baseline, two alternative 2055 outcomes" rather than a
# three-step timeline.
x_positions = {"existing_2027": 0.0, "no_build_2055": 1.6, "rtp_2055": 2.6}
x = [x_positions[s] for s in scenario_order]
for i, mode in enumerate(("bike", "transit")):
    vals = (
        region[region["mode"] == mode]
        .set_index("scenario")["pct_near_facility"]
        .reindex(scenario_order)
        * 100
    )
    offset = (i - 0.5) * bar_width
    ax.bar([xi + offset for xi in x], vals, width=bar_width, color=MODE_COLORS[mode], zorder=3)
    for xi, v in zip(x, vals):
        ax.text(
            xi + offset,
            v + 3,
            f"{v:.0f}%",
            ha="center",
            va="bottom",
            fontsize=10.5,
            fontfamily="Poppins SemiBold",
            color=MODE_COLORS[mode],
        )

# Divider + bracket reinforce the same point visually: a dotted line splits
# the baseline from the 2055 pair, and a bracket spans only the pair it
# actually groups.
divider_x = (x_positions["existing_2027"] + x_positions["no_build_2055"]) / 2
ax.axvline(divider_x, color=INK, alpha=0.15, linestyle=":", linewidth=1, zorder=1)
bracket_left, bracket_right = (
    x_positions["no_build_2055"] - bar_width,
    x_positions["rtp_2055"] + bar_width,
)
ax.plot(
    [bracket_left, bracket_left, bracket_right, bracket_right],
    [103, 106, 106, 103],
    color=INK,
    linewidth=1,
    zorder=4,
)
ax.text(
    (bracket_left + bracket_right) / 2,
    108,
    "2055 — two alternative futures",
    ha="center",
    va="bottom",
    fontsize=9.5,
    style="italic",
    color=INK,
)

ax.set_xticks(x)
ax.set_xticklabels([scenario_labels[s] for s in scenario_order], fontsize=11, color=INK)
ax.set_xlim(x_positions["existing_2027"] - 0.6, x_positions["rtp_2055"] + 0.6)
ax.set_ylim(0, 118)
ax.set_yticks([])
for side in ("top", "right", "left"):
    ax.spines[side].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["bottom"].set_color(INK)
ax.spines["bottom"].set_linewidth(1)
ax.tick_params(length=0)

fig.text(
    0.03,
    0.95,
    "Bike access far outpaces transit, in every scenario",
    ha="left",
    va="top",
    fontsize=15,
    fontfamily="Poppins SemiBold",
    color=INK,
)
fig.text(
    0.03,
    0.88,
    f"Share of WFRC-region population within 1/4 mile of a facility — today, {bike_existing * 100:.0f}% for bike vs {transit_existing * 100:.0f}% for transit",
    ha="left",
    va="top",
    fontsize=10.5,
    color="#55595e",
)
# Poppins has no glyph for "●" (renders as tofu) -- fall back to DejaVu Sans
# for just the bullet markers, keep Poppins for the labels.
fig.text(
    0.03, 0.80, "●", ha="left", va="top", fontsize=13, color=MODE_COLORS["bike"],
    fontfamily="DejaVu Sans",
)
fig.text(0.05, 0.805, "Bike", ha="left", va="top", fontsize=10.5, color=INK)
fig.text(
    0.115, 0.80, "●", ha="left", va="top", fontsize=13, color=MODE_COLORS["transit"],
    fontfamily="DejaVu Sans",
)
fig.text(0.135, 0.805, "Transit", ha="left", va="top", fontsize=10.5, color=INK)
fig.text(
    0.03,
    0.03,
    "Source: WFRC Transportation Choices analysis (v10)",
    ha="left",
    fontsize=8.5,
    color="#8a8f98",
    style="italic",
)

fig.savefig(PATHS["output"] / "region_pct.png", facecolor=fig.get_facecolor(), dpi=150)
plt.show()
```
